title: Almond frangipane tart (galette des rois-style)
summary: Two rounds of almond pastry sealed around a rum-scented frangipane and scored in the classic pattern; a low-carb nod to the French Epiphany cake.
steps: Pulse the almond flour, psyllium, xanthan gum, erythritol and salt in a food processor. Add the butter and egg and pulse until the dough forms. Divide in two, flatten each into a disc and chill 30 minutes.
Beat the butter and erythritol for the frangipane until fluffy, then the egg, almond flour and both extracts. Chill while you roll the pastry.
Roll each disc between parchment to a 23 cm (9 in) round. Slide one round, on its parchment, onto a baking sheet.
Spread the frangipane over it, leaving a 2 cm (3/4 in) border. Hide a whole almond in it if you like. Brush the border with water, lay the second round on top and press the edges firmly to seal.
Whisk the yolk with the water and brush the top. Chill 20 minutes, brush again, then score a curved sunburst pattern lightly with a knife tip, and cut a small steam hole in the centre.
Heat the oven to 180 °C (355 °F) and bake 30–35 minutes, until deep golden. Cool at least 30 minutes; serve warm or at room temperature.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter gives a slightly crumblier pastry and a softer frangipane; chill the assembled tart well before baking.
tips: This is a short almond pastry, not puff pastry: it will be tender and crumbly rather than flaky.
Warn guests if you hide a whole almond in place of the traditional fève.

origin.history: Sharing a cake with a hidden bean at Epiphany, the finder becoming king or queen for the day, is a custom with medieval roots in France and elsewhere in Europe. In Paris and northern France the cake became a puff-pastry galette filled with frangipane, an almond cream; in the south a brioche ring is more usual. Porcelain charms called fèves later replaced the dried bean.
